question: Should OpenClaw add a native child-session context-pressure contract, and if so should it warn only, notify the parent/operator, or trigger recovery actions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but threshold defaults, parent identity, operator target, and automatic recovery semantics are product/API decisions with config and compatibility impact.

options.title: Define a narrow context-pressure contract
options.body: Add reporting and notification semantics for saturated child sessions first, then gate any recovery action behind explicit maintainer-chosen policy.

options.title: Fold into broader subagent recovery work
options.body: Track this under an existing subagent stall/circuit-breaker direction if maintainers want one combined reliability policy instead of a context-specific path.

options.title: Leave to external fleet monitoring
options.body: Treat saturation alerts as operator-owned monitoring for now and document the existing status/session data surfaces instead of adding core behavior.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow context-pressure contract
recommendation.body: Add reporting and notification semantics for saturated child sessions first, then gate any recovery action behind explicit maintainer-chosen policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session/subagent path history and the product-boundary decision make steipete the best available routing owner from the inspected history.
